question.text: Under the SEBI AML Master Circular, intermediaries must classify clients into risk categories. What are these categories?

explanation.text: The Logic: The SEBI Master Circular states that the factors of risk perception should enable classification of clients into low, medium and high risk. Clients of Special Category (CSCs) may be classified even higher if warranted. The Trap: All the distractors describe tiered classification systems, but the specific terminology used by SEBI is low, medium and high risk. Note: The CSC category sits on top of this baseline classification and can attract a higher risk rating than 'high'.
